title: Orchestrate safe dependency bumps across Python/JS/Go SDKs with compatibility matrix and canary plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a coordinated, low-risk plan to bump transitive and direct dependencies across our Python, JS, and Go SDKs, prune deprecated API surface, and ensure runtime compatibility for hosted and dedicated deployments. This ticket covers: dependency inventory, compatibility matrix, automated CI/QA guardrails, canary rollout plan, deprecation notices, and follow-up cleanup PRs.

Motivation:
Recent incidents and benchmark spikes (see runtime-1.19 incident runbook) revealed that uncoordinated dependency upgrades produce subtle regressions (transport timeouts, JSON encoding differences, minor TLS handshakes). Many repos have drifted (different versions of http libraries, gRPC, JSON encoders), causing incompatibility between client bundles and server routing/telemetry. A cross-language, test-driven approach will reduce flakiness and long-term maintenance cost.

Scope:
- Python: bump requests, httpx, protobuf, pydantic (where used by examples), and pin typing-extensions to a single compatible range.
- JS: bump node-fetch/fetch polyfills, undici, typescript dev deps, and our bundler plugin versions.
- Go: bump go modules: net/http helpers, protobuf, grpc, and update CI to use Go 1.21 minimum.
- Remove deprecated API params and map backwards-compatible shims where strictly necessary for a single release.
- Publish compatibility matrix that maps SDK versions -> supported server runtime versions and recommended pin ranges.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs build cleanly in CI on head and on pinned docker images.
- Cross-language integration tests pass: auth flow, streaming generation, embeddings, and structured output.
- No change in tail P95 latency >5% in canary group; token-cost regression <1% on internal benchmark suite.
- Deprecation notices added to changelogs and a migration guide published to Docs.
- Rollout automation: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error budget breach.

Implementation plan / notes:
1) Inventory: run dependency scanner across mono-repo and client repos; produce spreadsheet and proposed target versions. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SDK-Dep-Inventory (internal).
2) Compatibility matrix: draft as CSV and check against server runtime-1.20 and 1.19.
3) Parallel branch work: create per-language feature branches that only bump deps + update unit/integration tests, then open cross-repo PRs for simultaneous merge.
4) CI/QA: add smoke integration job that runs a small local server with runtime-1.20 image and exercises streaming + embeddings. Fail CI on any serialization schema drift.
5) Canary rollout: use console rollout config; set initial canary at 5% for 48h, monitor errors, latencies, and cost. Preferred rollback condition: error rate spike >1% absolute or P95 tail latency degradation >10%.
6) Post-merge cleanup: remove temporary shims, update examples, bump docs.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Pinning versions tightly reduces unexpected breakage but increases patch work; we choose semver-minor bounds with a 3-month review cadence.
- Shimming deprecated params increases surface area; prefer to keep shims for a single release with strong telemetry on usage to force client updates.
- Some older enterprise customers pin older runtime versions; matrix must clearly state which SDK versions are incompatible.

Links & artifacts:
- Draft compatibility matrix: https://docs.internal.redwood.com/sdk-compat-matrix-draft (internal)
- PRs: will list in comments as opened
- Benchmarks dashboard: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.com/bench/sdk-deps-bump-canary

Rollback plan:
- Immediate rollback via console: route canary traffic back to previous SDK runtime variant and force downgrade of SDK packages in the hosted bundle if a high-severity issue is traced to the dependency bump.

Longer-term follow-ups (outside this ticket):
- Automate monthly dependency scan alerts into Slack.
- Add a lightweight cross-SDK e2e harness that runs against nightly runtime images.

Security review required: false

2025-03-08 - QA: Canary harness added to CI. Integration test failures (streaming boundary conditions) traced to undici major behavior change; opened ENG-182010-js-undici-fix (sub-issue). Will gate JS bump on that fix.
